trig.title: Right-triangle trig — height from angle and hypotenuse
trig.question: A zip-line cable is anchored to the top of a platform and makes a $48°$ angle with the level ground. The cable is $35\text{ ft}$ long. To the nearest tenth of a foot, how high above the ground is the anchor point at the top of the platform?

solution_steps.title: Understand the Setup
solution_steps.description:
A zip-line cable stretches from the top of a platform down to the ground, forming a **right triangle**. The cable itself is the **hypotenuse** ($35\text{ ft}$), the angle between the cable and the ground is $48°$, and the platform height is the **side opposite** that angle — which is exactly what we want.

Whenever you know the hypotenuse and an angle, and you want the **opposite** side, the tool is $\sin$:
$$\sin(\theta) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$$

solution_steps.title: Set Up the Equation
solution_steps.description:
Plug the known values into the sine ratio, then solve for the height by multiplying both sides by $35$:
$$\sin(48°) = \frac{\text{height}}{35}$$
$$\text{height} = 35 \times \sin(48°)$$

linear.title: Multi-step linear equation — solve for x
linear.question:
Solve for $x$:
$$\frac{3(x-2)}{4} - \frac{x+1}{3} = 2.$$
Show all steps and box your answer.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Problem
solution_steps.description: We have one equation with two fractions and need to find $x$. Fractions make algebra messy, so the key insight is to **eliminate all denominators at once** by multiplying every term by the **Least Common Denominator (LCD)**. The denominators are $4$ and $3$, so $\text{LCD} = 12$. This instantly clears both fractions and leaves a simple linear equation.

solution_steps.title: Multiply Every Term by 12
solution_steps.description:
Multiply both sides of the equation by $12$:
$$12 \cdot \frac{3(x-2)}{4} - 12 \cdot \frac{x+1}{3} = 12 \cdot 2$$
$12 \div 4 = 3$ and $12 \div 3 = 4$, so the fractions vanish cleanly:
$$3 \cdot 3(x-2) - 4(x+1) = 24$$
$$9(x-2) - 4(x+1) = 24$$

solution_steps.title: Distribute & Simplify
solution_steps.description:
Expand each group by distributing:
$$9x - 18 - 4x - 4 = 24$$
Combine the $x$-terms ($9x - 4x$) and the constants ($-18 - 4$):
$$5x - 22 = 24$$

solution_steps.title: Isolate $x$
solution_steps.description:
Add $22$ to both sides to move the constant:
$$5x = 46$$
Divide both sides by $5$:
$$x = \frac{46}{5}$$

solution_steps.title: Verify the Solution
solution_steps.description:
Substitute $x = \frac{46}{5}$ back into the original equation.

**Left side:**
$$\frac{3\!\left(\frac{46}{5}-2\right)}{4} - \frac{\frac{46}{5}+1}{3} = \frac{3 \cdot \frac{36}{5}}{4} - \frac{\frac{51}{5}}{3} = \frac{\frac{108}{5}}{4} - \frac{51}{15} = \frac{108}{20} - \frac{51}{15}$$
$$= \frac{27}{5} - \frac{17}{5} = \frac{10}{5} = 2 \checkmark$$
Matches the right side, confirming our answer.

matrix.title: Matrix multiplication — compute product AB
matrix.question:
Compute the matrix product $AB$, where
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \quad \text{and} \quad B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}.$$
Give each entry of the resulting $2 \times 2$ matrix.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Setup
solution_steps.description:
Matrix multiplication works by taking each **row of A** and pairing it with each **column of B** — multiplying matching entries and summing them. The result lives in position $(i, j)$ of the output, produced by row $i$ of $A$ and column $j$ of $B$.

For two $2 \times 2$ matrices, there are **four entries** to compute:
$$AB = \begin{pmatrix} A_{\text{row1}} \cdot B_{\text{col1}} & A_{\text{row1}} \cdot B_{\text{col2}} \\ A_{\text{row2}} \cdot B_{\text{col1}} & A_{\text{row2}} \cdot B_{\text{col2}} \end{pmatrix}$$
Each "$\cdot$" means multiply element-by-element then add — this is called the **dot product**.

solution_steps.title: Assemble the Result
solution_steps.description:
Place the four computed entries back into the $2 \times 2$ grid:
$$AB = \begin{pmatrix} 11 & 24 \\ 9 & 6 \end{pmatrix}$$
